Colder shelves (-15 °C, -25 °C) dry slower: 0.2 Torr/-15 °C takes 29.35 h; -25 °C slower still, so none can beat -5 °C. Fastest complete-drying recipe within both constraints: 0.2 Torr chamber pressure with -5 °C shelf setpoint, predicted primary-drying completion 17.79 h, thermal margin -0.698 °C, capacity margin -0.105 kg/h. **Fastest feasible recipe: 0.2 Torr chamber pressure with −5 °C shelf setpoint — predicted complete drying in 17.79 h, thermal margin −0.70 °C below the critical bottom temperature, capacity margin −0.105 kg/h below the equipment line.** Assessment saved as a review draft (synthetic example, authored simulator inputs — not experimental validation, not an approval).

**Why this pair.** All three +10 °C shelf candidates dry fastest (10.97–13.02 h) but their returned vial-bottom temperatures peak above the −18 °C critical limit (−17.07 °C at 0.05 Torr, −15.82 °C at 0.1 Torr, −13.84 °C at 0.2 Torr), so none is feasible. At −5 °C shelf all three pressures dry fully and comply: 0.2 Torr is fastest (17.79 h, max bottom −18.70 °C), ahead of 0.1 Torr (18.85 h, −20.58 °C) and 0.05 Torr (19.67 h, −21.78 °C). The colder shelves cannot beat this: 0.2 Torr at −15 °C took 29.35 h, and −25 °C is slower still.

**Equipment-line check (derived from returned values).** Peak returned flux 0.6312 kg/h per m², product area 3.14 cm² = 0.000314 m², 398 vials → whole-batch peak 0.79 kg/h versus the line at 0.2 Torr: −0.182 + 11.7 × 0.2 = 0.998 kg/h. Thermal margin: −18.6979 − (−18.0) = −0.698 °C.

Both margins are thin: thermal margin is less than 0.7 °C and uses returned solver nodes only (no continuous-maximum guarantee), and the batch demand sits ~0.1 kg/h under the line at peak. A denser solver grid or a slightly colder shelf (−5 °C → −15 °C costs ~11.6 h) would confirm robustness; the draft record lists the exact native result IDs for review.
